evidence: accountable evidence: mix.AttributeFault walks a signed shuffle chain and names the mixer that signed an unsound round; mix.VerifyFaultReport re-derives the fault from the transcript so a third party confirms it without trusting the reporter
blame soundness: an honest three-round chain produces no report, a fabricated report against it does not verify, and a genuine report re-pointed at an innocent neighbour is rejected

non-attribution where the protocol cannot attribute: a forged receipt marks the impersonated mixer as a victim rather than a culprit; broken linkage is charged to the chain assembler because either neighbour could cause it, and is checked before soundness so a mixer handed the wrong input is not accused of an unsound round; an empty transcript is a fault with no one to blame
malformed input: TestHostileDatagramsAreRejectedForTheRightReason; strictjson refuses ambiguous encodings before decoding; mutation and truncation sweeps over every published conformance vector
replay and duplication: chain replay across epoch and committee refused, hop replay window, decoder duplicate deduplication before any budget is charged

drop and delay without private-dependent recovery: the one-second burst ceiling is asserted on every captured world, and the WAN campaign's emission counts are exactly equal across worlds on every host

availability accountability implemented: mix.RoundSchedule fixes a round's deadline from the epoch timetable and the round's position, taking a slot index rather than a batch so a deadline cannot vary with batch contents; each observer signs its own non-receipt bound to committee, epoch, batch, round, deadline and accused; a report is a quorum of statements from distinct certified operators

availability blame cannot be a weapon: below quorum establishes nothing, one operator repeating its own statement does not reach quorum, an uncertified key does not count, an operator cannot report itself, and an accusation cannot be re-pointed at an innocent member. Four mutants were run against the suite and each is killed by a distinct test

refutation names its signers: the accused answers with its own sound round for that exact position, and because every statement is individually signed the refutation names the observers the transcript contradicts. Answering with a round from another position, another mixer's round, or an unsound round all fail

availability observation holds the privacy boundary at the testnet: live/availability judges every certified operator at every deadline rather than only the failures, so report volume cannot track operator load; the deadline comes from the schedule rather than a clock; two observations of one position are byte-identical; and CI holds the package's transitive graph to mix and topology so it cannot reach a query, a basin or a reconstruction

an operator disappearing changes nothing the surviving peer sees: with a two-peer rotation and one operator's socket absent, the survivor receives exactly its half rather than the vanished peer's share, the sender counts every scheduled emission as sent, and the outage world is identical whether the node is idle or busy. The no-reroute claim is the one that matters: rerouting would announce the disappearance to whoever is still up, by giving them more traffic

selective failure is now measured rather than untested, and the result is a limit rather than a defence: an operator starving a quorum of peers is reported exactly as a total failure is, but one starving fewer is invisible, and rotating which minority it starves never accumulates because each report is scoped to one position
blockers: no active-adversary fault injection at the live boundary: the fault attribution is exercised against constructed transcripts, not against a running committee where a mixer misbehaves mid-session. That needs the distributed deposit path (PROD-17) to exist first

availability reports establish that work did not arrive at the observers, never that it was withheld: asynchrony makes those indistinguishable and the implementation says so rather than claiming otherwise. Deciding what a deployment does with a report is governance work that is not built
the observer is unit-tested against a delivery source, not run against a live committee where an operator actually stops: that needs the same live boundary PROD-17 does

selective failure below the observer quorum is undetectable by this mechanism and cannot be fixed by lowering the quorum: the same threshold is what stops a coalition evicting an honest operator, so one accuser must never be enough. An operator willing to starve a minority every round, rotating which minority, is invisible to availability reporting indefinitely. Detecting it needs something this design does not have -- cross-round accumulation, which would itself need a rule for whose accusations count over time

reproducible model identity implemented (nomad-semantic-basins a96d821, basin/attest.go): a service is fingerprinted over a fixed public probe set, and verification refuses when its basins move. The fingerprint is over quantized basins rather than raw vectors on purpose -- float output differs in the last bits between runs and hardware without meaning anything, while a change large enough to move a basin is by definition a change that moves what a reader fetches

the attestation refuses to fingerprint nothing: fewer than four probes, a repeated probe, an empty probe and a service that answers every input identically are all rejected when the attestation is made rather than discovered later matching everything. Verification fails closed on an unknown version, a malformed digest, an edited or reordered probe set, a different quantizer seed, a service that errors and a nil embedder

the artefact carries no private state: probes are fixed public strings, exported so an operator can see what is sent to their service, and a test embeds unrelated reader queries between two attestations and requires the digest not to move
blockers: sandbox, authenticated IPC and model attestation

attestation establishes reproducibility, never authenticity: the embedding service is a separate process and nothing it says about which model it loaded can be checked from outside. A service willing to lie about its model is willing to lie about a hash of it. What is detected is change, which is the property the system depends on, and the implementation says so rather than claiming more

the service is still only bounded, not sandboxed: no OS sandbox, no mutual IPC authentication (the API key authenticates the client to the service, not the service to the client), and no attempted-egress packet capture

docs/DATA_RETENTION.md documents what macOS retains outside the app's control, with the command to clear each where one exists: crash reports (which record thread stacks as raw machine words and so can carry object fragments, written outside the container and surviving uninstall), local APFS snapshots and Time Machine, the Spotlight index, unified log entries, and swap

the uninstaller is cross-checked against the source rather than trusted: every directory name the Swift sources construct must appear in the script, the bundle identifier must match Info.plist, and the retained-data list must stay in both the script and the document. Each check was verified by introducing the drift it exists to catch

update verification with anti-rollback implemented and adversarially tested (Nomad-browser/update, 9121eca): rollback, equivocation and substitution each refused by name; unknown manifest versions refused rather than downgraded; a manifest signed by an untrusted key refused although it verifies under its own; an unreadable watermark refuses the install rather than being treated as absent, which is what stops anyone who can corrupt one file from switching rollback protection off

the updater is architecturally unable to grant the networkless browser network access: it verifies bytes the user already has and fetches nothing, and a dependency test fails if its transitive graph gains net, net/http, net/url or os/exec -- verified by adding an http import and confirming the test fires

disaster-recovery exercise that runs: live/node/recovery_test.go destroys each piece of a node's durable state in turn -- raw cache, hop sequence, topology watermark, and the combination -- and records what the code does. deploy/RECOVERY.md is written from what it measured rather than from what recovery ought to look like

the exercise's finding: a hop sequence file restored from backup moves the counter backwards and the node reissues numbers its peers have already seen. Measured in the unit exercise (sender emitted 18 cells, 0 local drops, receiver refused 17 as replays) and again end to end in the drill with shipped binaries (sender sent 99 cells, 0 local drops, passed --check-health; peer refused 80 replays). The sender cannot detect it at all; the only signal is a peer's replay_rejected, and the runbook is built around that

incident drill that runs: scripts/incident-drill.sh builds the real binaries, bootstraps three operators on loopback and works two scenarios with a pass or fail for each -- a node present and not working, and the sequence rollback. It runs in CI rather than on request, because a runbook whose drill has not been run since the code moved is a document about an older system

second drill finding: a stopped node that is resumed exits rather than carrying on, because it missed its lateness budget and a fixed-cadence sender refuses a catch-up burst. Recovery from a hang is therefore a restart and not a resume, which the runbook now says. That is the privacy invariant costing availability on purpose

the drill found two defects in itself before it found any in the system, both recorded: it asked only one peer for replay_rejected when the signed plan decides who hears whom, and it backed up and restored the sequence file either side of a single restart, where the bytes are identical and the restore does nothing. Both made it report that the documented signal never appears
blockers: no 30-day soak. Every figure in SLO.md comes from tests measured in seconds, in a container, alongside other work: they establish that a bound exists and is enforced and say nothing about drift, leaks or degradation over weeks, which is what a soak is for. This cannot be compressed and is why the criterion is not MET
no capacity targets: cells per second per operator, objects per epoch and concurrent publishers have no numbers, because none has been measured at a scale where the number would mean anything
no regional-failure exercise: the drill is three processes on one host's loopback. Node loss is exercised, regional failure is not, and that needs multi-region infrastructure (EB-3)
no incident history: these objectives have been tested only by exercises this project designed and ran
blocked on EB-4: independent cryptographic, systems, browser and privacy assessors. This criterion cannot be self-approved, and a subagent review is QA rather than independence

evidence: the two-person release process is a control rather than a document: a release manifest carries approvals, and Nomad-browser update.Decode refuses one without signatures from at least two distinct trusted approver keys. The refusal happens on the machine that would otherwise install the release, which is the one party with no incentive to skip the step

adversarial, mutation-verified: fewer than two approvals refused; two approvals from the same key refused, because one person signing twice is one person; an approval from an untrusted key refused; a build whose trusted set is one key or one key listed twice refused before a manifest is read; approvals do not transfer between releases, covering version, channel, artifact name, digest and size. Five mutations of the rule are all caught

the manifest format is v2 and Sign is gone: a release is not signed by the project, it is approved by people. Prepare builds the manifest, Approve adds one person's signature, and Approve takes a single key on purpose because a function taking two at once would be a two-person process one person can run

exercised end to end with the shipped binary: two approvers verify, one trusted approver is refused with 'One person who can approve alone is not a two-person process', and a build with no keys refuses and names EB-6 and EB-7

rollback plan in Nomad-browser docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md: roll-forward only, because an updater that can move a user backwards is one an attacker can move backwards. It also records what cannot be solved -- a user already on a bad release cannot be reached, since the browser fetches nothing, and a compromised approver key has no revocation channel, so a build trusting exactly two keys cannot survive losing one
blockers: no monitored multi-operator beta: nothing has been given to users at all, which is the substance of this criterion and needs people (EB-4)
no release red team. An internal adversarial exercise is not one, and a subagent review is QA rather than independence
no second approver and no release keys: the mechanism is ready and exercised only against test keys, which the tool says out loud every time it is used that way (EB-6, EB-7)
two keys held by one person satisfy every check the code makes. Key custody is what makes this a two-person process and it is an operational property, not a cryptographic one
